data.subtitle: How AI sees, hears and speaks

scenes.text: Modal just means a type of data, like text, images, audio or video. [1] So a multimodal AI is one that can understand more than one type, and often create more than one type too. It can [2] see images, [3] hear audio, [4] and speak, or even draw.

data.definition: AI that understands and creates more than one kind of data: text, images, audio and video.

scenes.text: So how does one model understand a photo? [1] You give it a picture, say, of your fridge. [2] First, the image is cut into small patches, like tiles. [3] Each patch is turned into numbers, just like word tokens. [4] Now the image and your question sit side by side, as one long sequence, [5] and the model reads both together, and answers in words.

So what can you do with it? [1] Point your camera at a maths problem, and get step by step help. [2] Snap a menu in another language, and get it translated instantly. [3] Or just talk to it live, and it replies in a natural voice.

data.heading: Try it yourself
items: Snap a problem, get the steps

scenes.text: Here's what today's models can handle. [1] Let's look at understanding versus creating. [2] Text, they can do both. [3] Images, they can read them, and many can create them. [4] Audio, they can listen, and speak. [5] And video, many can watch it, and some can now create short clips.

data.heading: What goes in, what comes out

scenes.text: And here's why this matters. [1] Earlier, you needed separate AIs, one for text, one for images, one for speech, all glued together. [2] Now, a single multimodal model handles them all, so it connects the dots, like what's in your photo, and what you actually asked.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think if AI can see a photo, it understands it perfectly. [2] Not always. It can misread small text, miscount objects, or misjudge what's happening. So for anything important, check it yourself.

data.myth: If AI can see a photo, it understands it perfectly.
data.fact: It can misread small text, miscount objects or misjudge a scene. Check anything important.
